data.falco_rules.local.yaml:
# ZT-XGuard custom Falco rules for controlled O-RAN Near-RT RIC xApps.
# These rules are intentionally scoped to the ricxapp namespace and to the
# main xApp containers only. Helper/init containers such as fetch-svid are
# excluded to reduce false positives.

- macro: ztx_xapp_namespace
  condition: k8s.ns.name = ricxapp


- list: ztx_main_xapp_containers
  items:
    - telemetry-monitor
    - qos-optimizer
    - traffic-analyzer
    - resource-optimizer
    - security-observer
    - kpimon-go
    - hw-go
    - hw-python
    - trafficxapp

- list: ztx_helper_containers
  items:
    - fetch-svid
    - spire-fetcher
    - istio-proxy
    - linkerd-proxy

- macro: ztx_controlled_xapp_pod
  condition: >
    (k8s.pod.name startswith "telemetry-monitor" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "qos-optimizer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "traffic-analyzer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "resource-optimizer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "security-observer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-kpimon-go" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-hw-go" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-hw-python" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-trafficxapp")

- macro: ztx_main_xapp_container
  condition: >
    container.name in (ztx_main_xapp_containers) and
    not container.name in (ztx_helper_containers)

- macro: ztx_in_container
  condition: container.id != host

- macro: ztx_controlled_xapp
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and ztx_xapp_namespace and ztx_controlled_xapp_pod and ztx_main_xapp_container

# --- Per-xApp identity and per-xApp allow-lists ---------------------------
# The rules below (unexpected_ric_probe, unexpected_peer_contact) are
# intentionally profile-specific, not shared like the rest of this file.
# Every xApp is forbidden from doing things like spawning a shell or
# touching the token file - that part of the profile is identical for all
# 5, so one shared rule per technique is correct and not lazy. But which
# RIC platform service and which peer xApp each one may contact is
# different per xApp (see k8s/profiles/*.json, the real, deployed source
# of truth for this) - a rule that just checks "did any xApp mention a
# ricxapp service" cannot tell a legitimate contact from an illegitimate
# one. These macros encode each xApp's own allow-list explicitly, exactly
# matching the profile actually mounted into that xApp's pod.

- macro: ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "telemetry-monitor"

- macro: ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "traffic-analyzer"

- macro: ztx_qos_optimizer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "qos-optimizer"

- macro: ztx_resource_optimizer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "resource-optimizer"

- macro: ztx_security_observer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "security-observer"

# The 4 non-dummy xApps (kpimon-go, hw-go, hw-python, trafficxapp) have no
# declared allow-list profile - they get every universal rule in this file,
# but are deliberately excluded from the peer/RIC-service allow-list rules
# (rules 6/7 below), which only make sense for an xApp with a known "who am
# I allowed to talk to" profile. kpimon-go in particular talks to RIC
# platform services constantly as its normal job (E2 registration,
# subscription, etc.) - applying rules 6/7 to it would flag its entire
# normal operation as "unexpected." ztx_profiled_xapp (not
# ztx_controlled_xapp) is what rules 6/7 use, so they stay scoped to only
# the 5 xApps that actually have a profile to check against.
- macro: ztx_profiled_xapp_pod
  condition: >
    (ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod or ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod or
     ztx_qos_optimizer_pod or ztx_resource_optimizer_pod or
     ztx_security_observer_pod)

- macro: ztx_profiled_xapp
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and ztx_xapp_namespace and ztx_profiled_xapp_pod and ztx_main_xapp_container

# RIC-platform-service destinations, one macro per real RIC service used
# anywhere across the 5 profiles (see ztx_common/runtime.py RIC_SERVICE_CANDIDATES
# for the same DNS names).
- macro: ztx_dest_e2mgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-e2mgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_prometheus
  condition: fd.sip.name = "r4-infrastructure-prometheus-server.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_submgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-submgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_rtmgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-rtmgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

# kpimon-go's own real RIC-platform contacts, taken from directly observing
# its live logs this session (E2 registration/subscription flow) - not a
# declared profile, since kpimon-go has none and is never modified. Used
# only by the informational "confirmed normal" rule below, never by a
# violation rule - kpimon-go is exempt from rules 6/7 (see ztx_profiled_xapp).
- macro: ztx_kpimon_go_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-kpimon-go"

- macro: ztx_dest_e2term
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-e2term-rmr-alpha.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_appmgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-appmgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_a1mediator
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-a1mediator-rmr.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

# fd.sip.name only supports exact match (=/!=), not contains/startswith -
# confirmed the hard way (Falco crashed on startup with "filter error:
# fd.*ip.name filter only supports '=' and '!=' operators"). So "any RIC
# platform service" has to be an explicit OR of every known one, not a
# domain-suffix wildcard.
- macro: ztx_ric_platform_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_dest_e2mgr or ztx_dest_prometheus or ztx_dest_e2term or
     ztx_dest_appmgr or ztx_dest_a1mediator or ztx_dest_submgr or ztx_dest_rtmgr)

# Peer-xApp destinations, one macro per dummy xApp's own Kubernetes Service.
- macro: ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor
  condition: fd.sip.name = "telemetry-monitor.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "traffic-analyzer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_qos_optimizer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "qos-optimizer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_resource_optimizer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "resource-optimizer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_peer_xapp_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor or ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer or
     ztx_dest_qos_optimizer or ztx_dest_resource_optimizer)

# Per-xApp allow-list, matching k8s/profiles/*.json exactly:
#   telemetry-monitor:   allowed_ric_services=[e2mgr]        allowed_peers=[]
#   traffic-analyzer:    allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[telemetry-monitor]
#   qos-optimizer:        allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[traffic-analyzer]
#   resource-optimizer:  allowed_ric_services=[prometheus]    allowed_peers=[]
#   security-observer:   allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[telemetry-monitor, traffic-analyzer, qos-optimizer, resource-optimizer]
- macro: ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
  condition: >
    (ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod and ztx_dest_e2mgr) or
    (ztx_resource_optimizer_pod and ztx_dest_prometheus)

- macro: ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp
  condition: >
    (ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod and ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor) or
    (ztx_qos_optimizer_pod and ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer) or
    (ztx_security_observer_pod and
     (ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor or ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer or
      ztx_dest_qos_optimizer or ztx_dest_resource_optimizer))

- list: ztx_shell_binaries
  items: [sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh, ash]

- list: ztx_sensitive_paths
  items:
    - /etc/shadow
    - /etc/sudoers
    - /etc/passwd

- list: ztx_sensitive_read_tools
  items:
    - cat
    - cp
    - tar
    - base64
    - hexdump
    - xxd
    - od
    - strings
    - grep
    - sed
    - awk
    - head
    - tail
    - less
    - more
    - openssl

- list: ztx_package_manager_binaries
  items: [apt, apt-get, apk, yum, dnf, rpm, dpkg, pip, pip3]

- list: ztx_permission_tamper_binaries
  items: [chmod, chown, setcap]

# 2026-07-24: both path macros below originally only checked fd.name,
# which is correct for fd-based syscalls (open/openat/openat2) but is
# EMPTY for path-based metadata syscalls - confirmed live via a debug rule
# dump: `chmod`/`fchmodat` reports its target via evt.arg.filename, with
# fd.name blank. Since ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper (used by both A11 and
# A12) explicitly includes chmod/fchmod/fchmodat/rename/renameat/unlink/
# unlinkat/chown/fchown/fchownat in its event-type list, a real chmod/
# rename/unlink-based tamper attempt against SVID material or xApp config
# was silently never matching either rule - the ONLY thing that fired was
# the separate, unrelated "Permission Tamper" rule (matches on exec of the
# chmod/chown/setcap BINARY itself, not the syscall's target path), which
# is a lower-severity SUSPICIOUS-tier signal. This is a structural gap
# affecting metadata-tamper detection for ALL 9 xApps, not just kpimon-go -
# found via kpimon-go's own N=50x8 evaluation run repeatedly showing 0
# successful containment for the config-tamper attack. Added
# evt.arg.filename as an alternate match.
- macro: ztx_svid_or_spire_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/etc/svid" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/spire" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/spire" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/etc/svid" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/run/spire" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/var/run/spire")

- macro: ztx_xapp_config_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/etc/xapp-profile" or
     fd.name startswith "/etc/config" or
     fd.name startswith "/opt/ric/config" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/etc/xapp-profile" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/etc/config" or
     evt.arg.filename startswith "/opt/ric/config")

- macro: ztx_exec_drop_path
  condition: >
    ((fd.name startswith "/tmp/" or
      fd.name startswith "/var/tmp/" or
      fd.name startswith "/dev/shm/") and
     (fd.name endswith ".sh" or
      fd.name endswith ".py" or
      fd.name endswith ".pl" or
      fd.name endswith ".rb" or
      fd.name endswith ".so" or
      fd.name endswith ".bin" or
      fd.name endswith ".run" or
      fd.name endswith ".out"))

- macro: ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  condition: >
    ((evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and evt.is_open_write=true) or
     evt.type in (rename, renameat, unlink, unlinkat, chmod, fchmod, fchmodat, chown, fchown, fchownat, setxattr, removexattr))

- macro: ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    evt.is_open_read=true and
    proc.name in (ztx_sensitive_read_tools)

- macro: ztx_k8s_api_target
  condition: >
    fd.sport=443 and
    (fd.sip=10.96.0.1 or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local" or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes.default" or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes")

# CoreDNS itself. Confirmed live from the cluster (2026-07-14):
# `kubectl get svc -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns` -> ClusterIP
# 10.96.0.10, the standard kubeadm default. Matched by raw IP, not
# fd.sip.name, because Falco cannot resolve a reverse-DNS name for the
# DNS server itself at the moment of first connecting to it - every
# xApp's DNS lookup (the UDP connect that happens before it can reach
# e2mgr/appmgr/a peer service by name) was showing up as
# fd.sip.name=null and getting misclassified as external egress before
# this macro existed. This is the exact case ztx_k8s_api_target already
# handles the same way for the K8s API server's own address.
- macro: ztx_dest_coredns
  condition: fd.sip=10.96.0.10

# 2026-07-24: kpimon-go's RMR library does a loopback self-probe during its
# own route-table bootstrap (confirmed live: connect attempts to
# 127.0.0.1:9, ::1:9, ::1:8090 immediately after "IP address is not able to
# resolve Interface... invalid network interface name" in its own startup
# log - port 9 is the classic discard port, consistent with a
# connectivity/interface self-test, not a real destination). This is
# traffic that never leaves the pod's own network namespace - it cannot be
# "external egress" under any definition, regardless of what it's actually
# testing internally.
- macro: ztx_dest_loopback
  condition: (fd.sip=127.0.0.1 or fd.sip="::1")

# CIDR notation in fd.sip in (...) is NOT valid Falco syntax either
# (confirmed the hard way: "unrecognized IPv4 address 10.244.0.0/16").
# Rather than guess a third IP-matching syntax, reuse the destination
# macros already proven to work (exact-match on fd.sip.name or fd.sip).
# "Known internal/expected traffic" = matches one of the destinations we
# already explicitly track. This is arguably the more correct Zero-Trust
# framing anyway: an xApp contacting some internal service we never
# enumerated is still worth flagging, not something to quietly wave
# through just because it happens to be inside the cluster.
#
# 2026-07-23: added raw-IP matching for every RIC platform service,
# alongside the existing by-name (fd.sip.name) macros above - confirmed
# live that kpimon-go's genuine RMR traffic to e2mgr/e2term/appmgr/
# a1mediator/submgr/rtmgr repeatedly shows fd.sip.name=null (same
# unresolved-at-connect-time phenomenon already documented for CoreDNS
# above, but affecting ALL RMR peers here, not just DNS itself, since RMR
# connects via raw IP and often never triggers a DNS lookup Falco could
# snoop at all). Confirmed via kubectl (2026-07-23) these are the live
# ClusterIPs (submgr's Services are headless/ClusterIP:None, so its pod IP
# is used instead - same durability caveat as any other pod-IP-based
# match, acceptable for a single-node cluster with low churn). This only
# widens the generic "is this genuinely external" catch-all
# (ztx_known_internal_dest, used by ZTX-A8 below) - it does NOT touch the
# separate, still-fully-enforced per-xApp allow-list rules 6/7
# (ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp/ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp), which
# correctly keep the 5 profiled demo xApps restricted to their own
# declared subset of these same services.
#
# 2026-07-23 (follow-up): also missing SDL/DBAAS (service-ricplt-dbaas-tcp,
# Redis, port 6379) - found live after fixing kpimon-go's DBAAS_SERVICE_HOST
# env var (was missing the .svc.cluster.local suffix, causing slow/failing
# DNS lookups that were ALSO contributing to its liveness-probe timeouts).
# Once DNS resolution started succeeding, its genuine Redis connections
# immediately showed up as new external_egress false positives (same
# fd.sip.name=null pattern, since it's also headless/ClusterIP:None - pod IP
# used instead, same durability caveat as submgr above). hw-go hits this
# too. Added its current backing pod IP alongside the others.
# 2026-07-24: the two pod-IP entries here (submgr, dbaas/redis - both
# headless/ClusterIP:None) had drifted stale after a cluster-wide pod
# churn event (Felix/Calico backend diagnostic that briefly broke pod
# networking cluster-wide and triggered mass pod restarts), causing
# kpimon-go's genuine SDL/DBAAS Redis traffic to misclassify as external
# egress and repeatedly auto-quarantine a perfectly healthy xApp - this is
# exactly the durability caveat this macro's own comments already warned
# about, now observed for real.
#
# Split into two groups instead of one flat list: stable ClusterIPs (real
# Services, never change) vs. headless-service backing-pod IPs (no stable
# Service IP exists, so the pod's own IP is used instead - drifts on every
# restart of that pod). The two single-IP macros below are each
# auto-reconciled by ztx_falco_rule_sync.py's background loop (started
# alongside app.py's other background threads) - do NOT hand-edit these
# two lines, they get overwritten the next time the reconciler runs
# (default every RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS) if it finds the backing pod's
# IP has changed.
# 2026-07-24 (follow-up): kpimon-go writes KPI metrics directly to
# InfluxDB (r4-influxdb-influxdb2, stable ClusterIP, port 80) as part of
# its own normal operation - confirmed live (fd.sip=10.109.93.154 on a
# genuine, unattacked pod immediately after a restore). Never previously
# enumerated at all (not even in the original stale list) - a real,
# previously-unknown gap, not a regression from the other fixes today.
- macro: ztx_ric_platform_stable_ips
  condition: >
    fd.sip in (10.110.255.182, 10.97.218.194, 10.106.73.114, 10.102.220.163,
               10.97.234.238, 10.102.61.81, 10.107.162.169, 10.103.185.176,
               10.100.239.72, 10.106.216.185, 10.98.35.144, 10.109.93.154)

- macro: ztx_dest_submgr_pod_ip
  condition: fd.sip=10.244.0.227

- macro: ztx_dest_dbaas_pod_ip
  condition: fd.sip=10.244.0.229

- macro: ztx_ric_platform_dest_by_ip
  condition: >
    (ztx_ric_platform_stable_ips or ztx_dest_submgr_pod_ip or ztx_dest_dbaas_pod_ip)

- macro: ztx_known_internal_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_ric_platform_dest or ztx_ric_platform_dest_by_ip or ztx_peer_xapp_dest or ztx_k8s_api_target or ztx_dest_coredns or ztx_dest_loopback)

- macro: ztx_container_runtime_socket_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/var/run/docker.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/docker.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/containerd/containerd.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/containerd/containerd.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/crio/crio.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/crio/crio.sock")

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected Shell
  desc: A shell was spawned inside a controlled xApp main container.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_shell_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_shell rule_id=ZTX-A1 xapp shell spawned
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name image=%container.image.repository)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, runtime, shell, compromise]

# 2026-07-23: kpimon-go's own container startup (glibc/Go runtime init doing
# a user-lookup style read of /etc/passwd, plus the entrypoint/init process
# reading its own mounted serviceaccount token - completely standard for any
# containerized, Kubernetes-aware app) was repeatedly triggering both rules
# below as CRITICAL false positives on every restart, confirmed directly:
# command=runc:[1:CHILD] init and command=entripoint.sh ./entripoint.sh
# [sic - that's the real observed binary name]. proc.vpid=1 is the
# container's own PID-1/entrypoint process as seen from its own PID
# namespace (confirmed valid Falco field via `falco --list`) - a universal,
# runtime-independent signal, not fragile to exact script naming, so it's
# included alongside the two specific observed cmdline patterns for
# belt-and-suspenders precision. This does not weaken detection of a real
# post-compromise file read: an attacker reading these files after gaining
# code execution (e.g. via a spawned shell, already caught by ZTX-A1) runs
# as a later, non-PID-1 process, which still matches these rules normally.
# 2026-07-24: this exemption only ever covered the bash entrypoint script
# itself (PID 1) - but kpimon-go's real work happens in two compiled
# binaries (kpimon, f1apServer) that the entrypoint forks as children
# (confirmed live via `ps`/`/proc` inspection: PID 1 = entripoint.sh, PID
# 7/8 = f1apServer/kpimon). Those binaries almost certainly load their own
# credentials (SVID cert via /etc/svid, possibly a ServiceAccount token if
# either does in-cluster K8s API calls) at THEIR OWN startup, which runs as
# a non-PID-1, non-entrypoint-named process - a case the old exemption
# never covered, meaning a legitimate first read from either binary could
# misfire as CRITICAL sensitive_file_access/serviceaccount_token_access.
# Added a second clause matching the real, observed parent-child
# relationship (proc.pname = the entrypoint, proc.name = one of the two
# known xApp binaries) - this still requires the read to come from a
# process directly forked by the container's own entrypoint, so a
# differently-parented process (e.g. a shell spawned by a compromised
# kpimon process to go read these files) still does NOT match and is
# still flagged. Known, inherent limit of syscall-level monitoring: this
# can't distinguish an in-process exploit (attacker code executing inside
# the already-running kpimon binary, no new process spawned) from a
# legitimate read, since both look identical at the syscall layer - not
# something this fix (or any purely syscall-based rule) can resolve.
- macro: ztx_kpimon_go_own_binaries
  condition: >
    (proc.pname in (entripoint.sh, entrypoint.sh) and
     proc.name in (kpimon, f1apServer))

- macro: ztx_container_init_process
  condition: >
    (proc.vpid = 1 or
     proc.cmdline startswith "runc:" or
     proc.cmdline contains "entripoint.sh" or
     proc.cmdline contains "entrypoint.sh" or
     ztx_kpimon_go_own_binaries)

- rule: ZTX xApp Sensitive File Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to open sensitive files.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    (fd.name in (ztx_sensitive_paths) or fd.name startswith "/root/.ssh" or fd.name contains "/.ssh/") and
    not ztx_container_init_process
  output: >
    ztx_signal=sensitive_file_access rule_id=ZTX-A2 xapp sensitive file access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, sensitive-file, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp ServiceAccount Token Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to read Kubernetes ServiceAccount token material.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.name startswith "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount" and
    not ztx_container_init_process
  output: >
    ztx_signal=serviceaccount_token_access rule_id=ZTX-A3 xapp serviceaccount token access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, serviceaccount, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp Suspicious Tool Execution
  desc: A controlled xApp main container started tools commonly used for probing, download, or data movement.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (curl, wget, nc, ncat, netcat, socat, ssh, scp, python, python3, perl, ruby)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=malicious_tool_execution rule_id=ZTX-A6 xapp suspicious tool execution
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, process, probing]

- rule: ZTX xApp External Egress Attempt
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted an outbound connection. External egress is forbidden by default for these xApps.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    not ztx_known_internal_dest
  output: >
    ztx_signal=external_egress rule_id=ZTX-A8 xapp external egress attempt
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport dest_ip=%fd.sip command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, egress, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected Peer xApp Contact
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp connected to another dummy xApp that is not on its own
    declared peer allow-list (see k8s/profiles/*.json for the per-xApp list).
    Replaces an earlier, naive version of this rule that only checked whether
    a ricxapp address appeared in the process command line, regardless of
    which xApp it was or whether that specific contact was expected -
    this version checks the real connection destination against the
    specific xApp's own profile.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_peer_xapp_dest and
    not ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_peer_contact rule_id=ZTX-A7 xapp unexpected peer contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, peer-contact, profile-violation]

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected RIC Service Contact
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp connected to a RIC platform service that is not on
    its own declared allow-list (see k8s/profiles/*.json for the per-xApp
    list) - e.g. traffic-analyzer, qos-optimizer, and security-observer
    have no RIC platform service allowed at all under the current profile
    design, so any RIC-platform contact from them is unexpected by
    definition.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_ric_platform_dest and
    not ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_ric_probe rule_id=ZTX-A17 xapp unexpected ric service contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, ric-service, profile-violation]

- rule: ZTX xApp SVID Or SPIFFE Material Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container accessed or tampered with SVID/SPIRE identity material.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_svid_or_spire_path and
    (ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper or ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=svid_material_access rule_id=ZTX-A11 xapp SVID or SPIFFE material access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name file_arg=%evt.arg.filename command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, spiffe, spire, svid]

- rule: ZTX xApp Profile Or Config Tamper
  desc: A controlled xApp main container modified verified profile or runtime config paths.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_xapp_config_path and
    ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  output: >
    ztx_signal=xapp_profile_or_config_tamper rule_id=ZTX-A12 xapp profile or config tamper
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name file_arg=%evt.arg.filename command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, config, integrity, tamper]

- rule: ZTX xApp Package Manager Execution
  desc: A controlled xApp main container executed a package manager binary.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_package_manager_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=package_manager_execution rule_id=ZTX-A13 xapp package manager execution
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, process, package-manager]

- rule: ZTX xApp Binary Drop In Writable Path
  desc: A controlled xApp main container wrote an executable-looking artifact into a writable execution path.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_exec_drop_path and
    ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  output: >
    ztx_signal=binary_drop rule_id=ZTX-A14 xapp binary or script drop
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, dropper, writable-path]

- rule: ZTX xApp Permission Tamper
  desc: A controlled xApp main container executed permission or ownership tampering binaries.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_permission_tamper_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=permission_tamper rule_id=ZTX-A15 xapp permission tamper
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, permissions, tamper]

- rule: ZTX xApp Kubernetes API Contact
  desc: A controlled xApp main container connected to the Kubernetes API service on port 443.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_k8s_api_target
  output: >
    ztx_signal=k8s_api_contact rule_id=ZTX-A16 xapp kubernetes api contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, kubernetes, api, network]

- rule: ZTX xApp Privileged Container Escape Attempt
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to access the container runtime socket (Docker/containerd/CRI-O) - a well-known container-escape and privilege-escalation vector (MITRE ATT&CK T1611, Escape to Host).
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2, connect) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_container_runtime_socket_path
  output: >
    ztx_signal=privileged_container_escape_attempt rule_id=ZTX-LM-03 xapp container escape attempt
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, container-escape, privilege-escalation, compromise]

# =====================================================================
# "Normal state" rules - audit-only confirmation of expected behavior.
# These are the positive mirror of rules above: they fire when something
# EXPECTED happens, not when something is wrong. All four are tagged
# ztx_signal=ignored on purpose - if this ever reaches the policy engine,
# ztx_state_engine.py already treats "ignored" as explicitly out of scope
# (state=IGNORED, no effect on the xApp's real security state), so these
# stay a pure Falco-side audit trail and never add noise to the decision
# engine. Falco itself cannot prove a negative ("nothing bad happened") -
# these rules only confirm that a specific expected action occurred.
# =====================================================================

- rule: ZTX xApp Identity Renewal Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    A helper container (fetch-svid/renew-svid) accessed SVID/SPIFFE
    identity material as expected - this is the legitimate, designed
    identity-renewal path, logged for audit completeness. Contrast with
    "ZTX xApp SVID Or SPIFFE Material Access" above, which fires (as a
    real violation) if the MAIN xApp container does this instead of the
    helper. Applies identically to all 9 xApps - every one has the same
    fetch-svid/renew-svid sidecar pattern.
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and
    ztx_xapp_namespace and
    ztx_controlled_xapp_pod and
    container.name in (fetch-svid, renew-svid) and
    ztx_svid_or_spire_path and
    (ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper or ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-01 xapp identity renewal confirmed normal
    (helper=%container.name file=%fd.name pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, normal, audit]

- rule: ZTX xApp In-Cluster Connection Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp made an outbound connection to one of the RIC
    platform services, peer xApps, or the Kubernetes API server we
    already explicitly track - the expected case, logged for audit
    completeness. Contrast with "ZTX xApp External Egress Attempt"
    above, which fires when a connection does NOT match any of these
    known destinations. Applies identically to all 9 xApps.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_known_internal_dest
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-02 xapp in-cluster connection confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, normal, audit]

- rule: ZTX xApp Expected Peer Or RIC Contact Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    One of the 5 profiled xApps connected to a peer or RIC service that
    IS on its own declared allow-list - the expected case, logged for
    audit completeness. Contrast with "ZTX xApp Unexpected Peer xApp
    Contact" and "ZTX xApp Unexpected RIC Service Contact" above, which
    fire on the disallowed case. One rule covers all 5, the same way
    rules 6/7 do - the per-xApp distinction lives in the
    ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp / ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
    macros already built for rules 6/7, reused here unchanged.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ((ztx_peer_xapp_dest and ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp) or
     (ztx_ric_platform_dest and ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp))
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-03 xapp expected peer or ric contact confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, normal, audit, profile-match]

- rule: ZTX kpimon-go Expected RIC Platform Contact Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    kpimon-go connected to a RIC platform service consistent with its
    real observed normal behavior (appmgr registration, e2term RMR
    routing, a1mediator RMR routing) - logged for audit completeness.
    Based on directly watching its real logs this session, not a
    declared profile - kpimon-go has no profile file and is never
    modified. kpimon-go does not get rules 6/7 (see ztx_profiled_xapp),
    so this is its only "confirmed normal" network signal.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_in_container and
    ztx_xapp_namespace and
    ztx_kpimon_go_pod and
    container.name = "kpimon-go" and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    (ztx_dest_e2term or ztx_dest_appmgr or ztx_dest_a1mediator)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-04 kpimon-go expected ric platform contact confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, kpimon-go, network, normal, audit]

annotations.kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-confi:
{"apiVersion":"v1","data":{"falco_rules.local.yaml":"# ZT-XGuard custom Falco rules for controlled O-RAN Near-RT RIC xApps.
# These rules are intentionally scoped to the ricxapp namespace and to the
# main xApp containers only. Helper/init containers such as fetch-svid are
# excluded to reduce false positives.

- macro: ztx_xapp_namespace
  condition: k8s.ns.name = ricxapp


- list: ztx_main_xapp_containers
  items:
    - telemetry-monitor
    - qos-optimizer
    - traffic-analyzer
    - resource-optimizer
    - security-observer
    - kpimon-go
    - hw-go
    - hw-python
    - trafficxapp

- list: ztx_helper_containers
  items:
    - fetch-svid
    - spire-fetcher
    - istio-proxy
    - linkerd-proxy

- macro: ztx_controlled_xapp_pod
  condition: >
    (k8s.pod.name startswith "telemetry-monitor" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "qos-optimizer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "traffic-analyzer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "resource-optimizer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "security-observer" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-kpimon-go" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-hw-go" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-hw-python" or
     k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-trafficxapp")

- macro: ztx_main_xapp_container
  condition: >
    container.name in (ztx_main_xapp_containers) and
    not container.name in (ztx_helper_containers)

- macro: ztx_in_container
  condition: container.id != host

- macro: ztx_controlled_xapp
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and ztx_xapp_namespace and ztx_controlled_xapp_pod and ztx_main_xapp_container

# --- Per-xApp identity and per-xApp allow-lists ---------------------------
# The rules below (unexpected_ric_probe, unexpected_peer_contact) are
# intentionally profile-specific, not shared like the rest of this file.
# Every xApp is forbidden from doing things like spawning a shell or
# touching the token file - that part of the profile is identical for all
# 5, so one shared rule per technique is correct and not lazy. But which
# RIC platform service and which peer xApp each one may contact is
# different per xApp (see k8s/profiles/*.json, the real, deployed source
# of truth for this) - a rule that just checks "did any xApp mention a
# ricxapp service" cannot tell a legitimate contact from an illegitimate
# one. These macros encode each xApp's own allow-list explicitly, exactly
# matching the profile actually mounted into that xApp's pod.

- macro: ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "telemetry-monitor"

- macro: ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "traffic-analyzer"

- macro: ztx_qos_optimizer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "qos-optimizer"

- macro: ztx_resource_optimizer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "resource-optimizer"

- macro: ztx_security_observer_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "security-observer"

# The 4 non-dummy xApps (kpimon-go, hw-go, hw-python, trafficxapp) have no
# declared allow-list profile - they get every universal rule in this file,
# but are deliberately excluded from the peer/RIC-service allow-list rules
# (rules 6/7 below), which only make sense for an xApp with a known "who am
# I allowed to talk to" profile. kpimon-go in particular talks to RIC
# platform services constantly as its normal job (E2 registration,
# subscription, etc.) - applying rules 6/7 to it would flag its entire
# normal operation as "unexpected." ztx_profiled_xapp (not
# ztx_controlled_xapp) is what rules 6/7 use, so they stay scoped to only
# the 5 xApps that actually have a profile to check against.
- macro: ztx_profiled_xapp_pod
  condition: >
    (ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod or ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod or
     ztx_qos_optimizer_pod or ztx_resource_optimizer_pod or
     ztx_security_observer_pod)

- macro: ztx_profiled_xapp
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and ztx_xapp_namespace and ztx_profiled_xapp_pod and ztx_main_xapp_container

# RIC-platform-service destinations, one macro per real RIC service used
# anywhere across the 5 profiles (see ztx_common/runtime.py RIC_SERVICE_CANDIDATES
# for the same DNS names).
- macro: ztx_dest_e2mgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-e2mgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_prometheus
  condition: fd.sip.name = "r4-infrastructure-prometheus-server.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_submgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-submgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_rtmgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-rtmgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

# kpimon-go's own real RIC-platform contacts, taken from directly observing
# its live logs this session (E2 registration/subscription flow) - not a
# declared profile, since kpimon-go has none and is never modified. Used
# only by the informational "confirmed normal" rule below, never by a
# violation rule - kpimon-go is exempt from rules 6/7 (see ztx_profiled_xapp).
- macro: ztx_kpimon_go_pod
  condition: k8s.pod.name startswith "ricxapp-kpimon-go"

- macro: ztx_dest_e2term
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-e2term-rmr-alpha.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_appmgr
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-appmgr-http.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_a1mediator
  condition: fd.sip.name = "service-ricplt-a1mediator-rmr.ricplt.svc.cluster.local"

# fd.sip.name only supports exact match (=/!=), not contains/startswith -
# confirmed the hard way (Falco crashed on startup with "filter error:
# fd.*ip.name filter only supports '=' and '!=' operators"). So "any RIC
# platform service" has to be an explicit OR of every known one, not a
# domain-suffix wildcard.
- macro: ztx_ric_platform_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_dest_e2mgr or ztx_dest_prometheus or ztx_dest_e2term or
     ztx_dest_appmgr or ztx_dest_a1mediator or ztx_dest_submgr or ztx_dest_rtmgr)

# Peer-xApp destinations, one macro per dummy xApp's own Kubernetes Service.
- macro: ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor
  condition: fd.sip.name = "telemetry-monitor.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "traffic-analyzer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_qos_optimizer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "qos-optimizer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_dest_resource_optimizer
  condition: fd.sip.name = "resource-optimizer.ricxapp.svc.cluster.local"

- macro: ztx_peer_xapp_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor or ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer or
     ztx_dest_qos_optimizer or ztx_dest_resource_optimizer)

# Per-xApp allow-list, matching k8s/profiles/*.json exactly:
#   telemetry-monitor:   allowed_ric_services=[e2mgr]        allowed_peers=[]
#   traffic-analyzer:    allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[telemetry-monitor]
#   qos-optimizer:        allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[traffic-analyzer]
#   resource-optimizer:  allowed_ric_services=[prometheus]    allowed_peers=[]
#   security-observer:   allowed_ric_services=[]              allowed_peers=[telemetry-monitor, traffic-analyzer, qos-optimizer, resource-optimizer]
- macro: ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
  condition: >
    (ztx_telemetry_monitor_pod and ztx_dest_e2mgr) or
    (ztx_resource_optimizer_pod and ztx_dest_prometheus)

- macro: ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp
  condition: >
    (ztx_traffic_analyzer_pod and ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor) or
    (ztx_qos_optimizer_pod and ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer) or
    (ztx_security_observer_pod and
     (ztx_dest_telemetry_monitor or ztx_dest_traffic_analyzer or
      ztx_dest_qos_optimizer or ztx_dest_resource_optimizer))

- list: ztx_shell_binaries
  items: [sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh, ash]

- list: ztx_sensitive_paths
  items:
    - /etc/shadow
    - /etc/sudoers
    - /etc/passwd

- list: ztx_sensitive_read_tools
  items:
    - cat
    - cp
    - tar
    - base64
    - hexdump
    - xxd
    - od
    - strings
    - grep
    - sed
    - awk
    - head
    - tail
    - less
    - more
    - openssl

- list: ztx_package_manager_binaries
  items: [apt, apt-get, apk, yum, dnf, rpm, dpkg, pip, pip3]

- list: ztx_permission_tamper_binaries
  items: [chmod, chown, setcap]

- macro: ztx_svid_or_spire_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/etc/svid" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/spire" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/spire")

- macro: ztx_xapp_config_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/etc/xapp-profile" or
     fd.name startswith "/etc/config" or
     fd.name startswith "/opt/ric/config")

- macro: ztx_exec_drop_path
  condition: >
    ((fd.name startswith "/tmp/" or
      fd.name startswith "/var/tmp/" or
      fd.name startswith "/dev/shm/") and
     (fd.name endswith ".sh" or
      fd.name endswith ".py" or
      fd.name endswith ".pl" or
      fd.name endswith ".rb" or
      fd.name endswith ".so" or
      fd.name endswith ".bin" or
      fd.name endswith ".run" or
      fd.name endswith ".out"))

- macro: ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  condition: >
    ((evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and evt.is_open_write=true) or
     evt.type in (rename, renameat, unlink, unlinkat, chmod, fchmod, fchmodat, chown, fchown, fchownat, setxattr, removexattr))

- macro: ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    evt.is_open_read=true and
    proc.name in (ztx_sensitive_read_tools)

- macro: ztx_k8s_api_target
  condition: >
    fd.sport=443 and
    (fd.sip=10.96.0.1 or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local" or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes.default" or
     fd.sip.name = "kubernetes")

# CoreDNS itself. Confirmed live from the cluster (2026-07-14):
# `kubectl get svc -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns` -> ClusterIP
# 10.96.0.10, the standard kubeadm default. Matched by raw IP, not
# fd.sip.name, because Falco cannot resolve a reverse-DNS name for the
# DNS server itself at the moment of first connecting to it - every
# xApp's DNS lookup (the UDP connect that happens before it can reach
# e2mgr/appmgr/a peer service by name) was showing up as
# fd.sip.name=null and getting misclassified as external egress before
# this macro existed. This is the exact case ztx_k8s_api_target already
# handles the same way for the K8s API server's own address.
- macro: ztx_dest_coredns
  condition: fd.sip=10.96.0.10

# 2026-07-24: kpimon-go's RMR library does a loopback self-probe during its
# own route-table bootstrap (confirmed live: connect attempts to
# 127.0.0.1:9, ::1:9, ::1:8090 immediately after "IP address is not able to
# resolve Interface... invalid network interface name" in its own startup
# log - port 9 is the classic discard port, consistent with a
# connectivity/interface self-test, not a real destination). This is
# traffic that never leaves the pod's own network namespace - it cannot be
# "external egress" under any definition, regardless of what it's actually
# testing internally.
- macro: ztx_dest_loopback
  condition: (fd.sip=127.0.0.1 or fd.sip="::1")

# CIDR notation in fd.sip in (...) is NOT valid Falco syntax either
# (confirmed the hard way: "unrecognized IPv4 address 10.244.0.0/16").
# Rather than guess a third IP-matching syntax, reuse the destination
# macros already proven to work (exact-match on fd.sip.name or fd.sip).
# "Known internal/expected traffic" = matches one of the destinations we
# already explicitly track. This is arguably the more correct Zero-Trust
# framing anyway: an xApp contacting some internal service we never
# enumerated is still worth flagging, not something to quietly wave
# through just because it happens to be inside the cluster.
#
# 2026-07-23: added raw-IP matching for every RIC platform service,
# alongside the existing by-name (fd.sip.name) macros above - confirmed
# live that kpimon-go's genuine RMR traffic to e2mgr/e2term/appmgr/
# a1mediator/submgr/rtmgr repeatedly shows fd.sip.name=null (same
# unresolved-at-connect-time phenomenon already documented for CoreDNS
# above, but affecting ALL RMR peers here, not just DNS itself, since RMR
# connects via raw IP and often never triggers a DNS lookup Falco could
# snoop at all). Confirmed via kubectl (2026-07-23) these are the live
# ClusterIPs (submgr's Services are headless/ClusterIP:None, so its pod IP
# is used instead - same durability caveat as any other pod-IP-based
# match, acceptable for a single-node cluster with low churn). This only
# widens the generic "is this genuinely external" catch-all
# (ztx_known_internal_dest, used by ZTX-A8 below) - it does NOT touch the
# separate, still-fully-enforced per-xApp allow-list rules 6/7
# (ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp/ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp), which
# correctly keep the 5 profiled demo xApps restricted to their own
# declared subset of these same services.
#
# 2026-07-23 (follow-up): also missing SDL/DBAAS (service-ricplt-dbaas-tcp,
# Redis, port 6379) - found live after fixing kpimon-go's DBAAS_SERVICE_HOST
# env var (was missing the .svc.cluster.local suffix, causing slow/failing
# DNS lookups that were ALSO contributing to its liveness-probe timeouts).
# Once DNS resolution started succeeding, its genuine Redis connections
# immediately showed up as new external_egress false positives (same
# fd.sip.name=null pattern, since it's also headless/ClusterIP:None - pod IP
# used instead, same durability caveat as submgr above). hw-go hits this
# too. Added its current backing pod IP alongside the others.
# 2026-07-24: the two pod-IP entries here (submgr, dbaas/redis - both
# headless/ClusterIP:None) had drifted stale after a cluster-wide pod
# churn event (Felix/Calico backend diagnostic that briefly broke pod
# networking cluster-wide and triggered mass pod restarts), causing
# kpimon-go's genuine SDL/DBAAS Redis traffic to misclassify as external
# egress and repeatedly auto-quarantine a perfectly healthy xApp - this is
# exactly the durability caveat this macro's own comments already warned
# about, now observed for real.
#
# Split into two groups instead of one flat list: stable ClusterIPs (real
# Services, never change) vs. headless-service backing-pod IPs (no stable
# Service IP exists, so the pod's own IP is used instead - drifts on every
# restart of that pod). The two single-IP macros below are each
# auto-reconciled by ztx_falco_rule_sync.py's background loop (started
# alongside app.py's other background threads) - do NOT hand-edit these
# two lines, they get overwritten the next time the reconciler runs
# (default every RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS) if it finds the backing pod's
# IP has changed.
- macro: ztx_ric_platform_stable_ips
  condition: >
    fd.sip in (10.110.255.182, 10.97.218.194, 10.106.73.114, 10.102.220.163,
               10.97.234.238, 10.102.61.81, 10.107.162.169, 10.103.185.176,
               10.100.239.72, 10.106.216.185, 10.98.35.144)

- macro: ztx_dest_submgr_pod_ip
  condition: fd.sip=10.244.0.99

- macro: ztx_dest_dbaas_pod_ip
  condition: fd.sip=10.244.0.191

- macro: ztx_ric_platform_dest_by_ip
  condition: >
    (ztx_ric_platform_stable_ips or ztx_dest_submgr_pod_ip or ztx_dest_dbaas_pod_ip)

- macro: ztx_known_internal_dest
  condition: >
    (ztx_ric_platform_dest or ztx_ric_platform_dest_by_ip or ztx_peer_xapp_dest or ztx_k8s_api_target or ztx_dest_coredns or ztx_dest_loopback)

- macro: ztx_container_runtime_socket_path
  condition: >
    (fd.name startswith "/var/run/docker.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/docker.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/containerd/containerd.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/containerd/containerd.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/var/run/crio/crio.sock" or
     fd.name startswith "/run/crio/crio.sock")

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected Shell
  desc: A shell was spawned inside a controlled xApp main container.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_shell_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_shell rule_id=ZTX-A1 xapp shell spawned
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name image=%container.image.repository)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, runtime, shell, compromise]

# 2026-07-23: kpimon-go's own container startup (glibc/Go runtime init doing
# a user-lookup style read of /etc/passwd, plus the entrypoint/init process
# reading its own mounted serviceaccount token - completely standard for any
# containerized, Kubernetes-aware app) was repeatedly triggering both rules
# below as CRITICAL false positives on every restart, confirmed directly:
# command=runc:[1:CHILD] init and command=entripoint.sh ./entripoint.sh
# [sic - that's the real observed binary name]. proc.vpid=1 is the
# container's own PID-1/entrypoint process as seen from its own PID
# namespace (confirmed valid Falco field via `falco --list`) - a universal,
# runtime-independent signal, not fragile to exact script naming, so it's
# included alongside the two specific observed cmdline patterns for
# belt-and-suspenders precision. This does not weaken detection of a real
# post-compromise file read: an attacker reading these files after gaining
# code execution (e.g. via a spawned shell, already caught by ZTX-A1) runs
# as a later, non-PID-1 process, which still matches these rules normally.
# 2026-07-24: this exemption only ever covered the bash entrypoint script
# itself (PID 1) - but kpimon-go's real work happens in two compiled
# binaries (kpimon, f1apServer) that the entrypoint forks as children
# (confirmed live via `ps`/`/proc` inspection: PID 1 = entripoint.sh, PID
# 7/8 = f1apServer/kpimon). Those binaries almost certainly load their own
# credentials (SVID cert via /etc/svid, possibly a ServiceAccount token if
# either does in-cluster K8s API calls) at THEIR OWN startup, which runs as
# a non-PID-1, non-entrypoint-named process - a case the old exemption
# never covered, meaning a legitimate first read from either binary could
# misfire as CRITICAL sensitive_file_access/serviceaccount_token_access.
# Added a second clause matching the real, observed parent-child
# relationship (proc.pname = the entrypoint, proc.name = one of the two
# known xApp binaries) - this still requires the read to come from a
# process directly forked by the container's own entrypoint, so a
# differently-parented process (e.g. a shell spawned by a compromised
# kpimon process to go read these files) still does NOT match and is
# still flagged. Known, inherent limit of syscall-level monitoring: this
# can't distinguish an in-process exploit (attacker code executing inside
# the already-running kpimon binary, no new process spawned) from a
# legitimate read, since both look identical at the syscall layer - not
# something this fix (or any purely syscall-based rule) can resolve.
- macro: ztx_kpimon_go_own_binaries
  condition: >
    (proc.pname in (entripoint.sh, entrypoint.sh) and
     proc.name in (kpimon, f1apServer))

- macro: ztx_container_init_process
  condition: >
    (proc.vpid = 1 or
     proc.cmdline startswith "runc:" or
     proc.cmdline contains "entripoint.sh" or
     proc.cmdline contains "entrypoint.sh" or
     ztx_kpimon_go_own_binaries)

- rule: ZTX xApp Sensitive File Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to open sensitive files.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    (fd.name in (ztx_sensitive_paths) or fd.name startswith "/root/.ssh" or fd.name contains "/.ssh/") and
    not ztx_container_init_process
  output: >
    ztx_signal=sensitive_file_access rule_id=ZTX-A2 xapp sensitive file access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, sensitive-file, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp ServiceAccount Token Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to read Kubernetes ServiceAccount token material.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.name startswith "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount" and
    not ztx_container_init_process
  output: >
    ztx_signal=serviceaccount_token_access rule_id=ZTX-A3 xapp serviceaccount token access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, serviceaccount, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp Suspicious Tool Execution
  desc: A controlled xApp main container started tools commonly used for probing, download, or data movement.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (curl, wget, nc, ncat, netcat, socat, ssh, scp, python, python3, perl, ruby)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=malicious_tool_execution rule_id=ZTX-A6 xapp suspicious tool execution
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, process, probing]

- rule: ZTX xApp External Egress Attempt
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted an outbound connection. External egress is forbidden by default for these xApps.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    not ztx_known_internal_dest
  output: >
    ztx_signal=external_egress rule_id=ZTX-A8 xapp external egress attempt
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport dest_ip=%fd.sip command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, egress, compromise]

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected Peer xApp Contact
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp connected to another dummy xApp that is not on its own
    declared peer allow-list (see k8s/profiles/*.json for the per-xApp list).
    Replaces an earlier, naive version of this rule that only checked whether
    a ricxapp address appeared in the process command line, regardless of
    which xApp it was or whether that specific contact was expected -
    this version checks the real connection destination against the
    specific xApp's own profile.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_peer_xapp_dest and
    not ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_peer_contact rule_id=ZTX-A7 xapp unexpected peer contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, peer-contact, profile-violation]

- rule: ZTX xApp Unexpected RIC Service Contact
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp connected to a RIC platform service that is not on
    its own declared allow-list (see k8s/profiles/*.json for the per-xApp
    list) - e.g. traffic-analyzer, qos-optimizer, and security-observer
    have no RIC platform service allowed at all under the current profile
    design, so any RIC-platform contact from them is unexpected by
    definition.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_ric_platform_dest and
    not ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
  output: >
    ztx_signal=unexpected_ric_probe rule_id=ZTX-A17 xapp unexpected ric service contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, ric-service, profile-violation]

- rule: ZTX xApp SVID Or SPIFFE Material Access
  desc: A controlled xApp main container accessed or tampered with SVID/SPIRE identity material.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_svid_or_spire_path and
    (ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper or ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=svid_material_access rule_id=ZTX-A11 xapp SVID or SPIFFE material access
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, spiffe, spire, svid]

- rule: ZTX xApp Profile Or Config Tamper
  desc: A controlled xApp main container modified verified profile or runtime config paths.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_xapp_config_path and
    ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  output: >
    ztx_signal=xapp_profile_or_config_tamper rule_id=ZTX-A12 xapp profile or config tamper
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, config, integrity, tamper]

- rule: ZTX xApp Package Manager Execution
  desc: A controlled xApp main container executed a package manager binary.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_package_manager_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=package_manager_execution rule_id=ZTX-A13 xapp package manager execution
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, process, package-manager]

- rule: ZTX xApp Binary Drop In Writable Path
  desc: A controlled xApp main container wrote an executable-looking artifact into a writable execution path.
  condition: >
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_exec_drop_path and
    ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper
  output: >
    ztx_signal=binary_drop rule_id=ZTX-A14 xapp binary or script drop
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, dropper, writable-path]

- rule: ZTX xApp Permission Tamper
  desc: A controlled xApp main container executed permission or ownership tampering binaries.
  condition: >
    evt.type in (execve, execveat) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    proc.name in (ztx_permission_tamper_binaries)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=permission_tamper rule_id=ZTX-A15 xapp permission tamper
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, filesystem, permissions, tamper]

- rule: ZTX xApp Kubernetes API Contact
  desc: A controlled xApp main container connected to the Kubernetes API service on port 443.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_k8s_api_target
  output: >
    ztx_signal=k8s_api_contact rule_id=ZTX-A16 xapp kubernetes api contact
    (user=%user.name dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: WARNING
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, kubernetes, api, network]

- rule: ZTX xApp Privileged Container Escape Attempt
  desc: A controlled xApp main container attempted to access the container runtime socket (Docker/containerd/CRI-O) - a well-known container-escape and privilege-escalation vector (MITRE ATT&CK T1611, Escape to Host).
  condition: >
    evt.type in (open, openat, openat2, connect) and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    ztx_container_runtime_socket_path
  output: >
    ztx_signal=privileged_container_escape_attempt rule_id=ZTX-LM-03 xapp container escape attempt
    (user=%user.name file=%fd.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, container-escape, privilege-escalation, compromise]

# =====================================================================
# "Normal state" rules - audit-only confirmation of expected behavior.
# These are the positive mirror of rules above: they fire when something
# EXPECTED happens, not when something is wrong. All four are tagged
# ztx_signal=ignored on purpose - if this ever reaches the policy engine,
# ztx_state_engine.py already treats "ignored" as explicitly out of scope
# (state=IGNORED, no effect on the xApp's real security state), so these
# stay a pure Falco-side audit trail and never add noise to the decision
# engine. Falco itself cannot prove a negative ("nothing bad happened") -
# these rules only confirm that a specific expected action occurred.
# =====================================================================

- rule: ZTX xApp Identity Renewal Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    A helper container (fetch-svid/renew-svid) accessed SVID/SPIFFE
    identity material as expected - this is the legitimate, designed
    identity-renewal path, logged for audit completeness. Contrast with
    "ZTX xApp SVID Or SPIFFE Material Access" above, which fires (as a
    real violation) if the MAIN xApp container does this instead of the
    helper. Applies identically to all 9 xApps - every one has the same
    fetch-svid/renew-svid sidecar pattern.
  condition: >
    ztx_in_container and
    ztx_xapp_namespace and
    ztx_controlled_xapp_pod and
    container.name in (fetch-svid, renew-svid) and
    ztx_svid_or_spire_path and
    (ztx_write_or_metadata_tamper or ztx_suspicious_sensitive_read)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-01 xapp identity renewal confirmed normal
    (helper=%container.name file=%fd.name pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, identity, normal, audit]

- rule: ZTX xApp In-Cluster Connection Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    A controlled xApp made an outbound connection to one of the RIC
    platform services, peer xApps, or the Kubernetes API server we
    already explicitly track - the expected case, logged for audit
    completeness. Contrast with "ZTX xApp External Egress Attempt"
    above, which fires when a connection does NOT match any of these
    known destinations. Applies identically to all 9 xApps.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_controlled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ztx_known_internal_dest
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-02 xapp in-cluster connection confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, normal, audit]

- rule: ZTX xApp Expected Peer Or RIC Contact Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    One of the 5 profiled xApps connected to a peer or RIC service that
    IS on its own declared allow-list - the expected case, logged for
    audit completeness. Contrast with "ZTX xApp Unexpected Peer xApp
    Contact" and "ZTX xApp Unexpected RIC Service Contact" above, which
    fire on the disallowed case. One rule covers all 5, the same way
    rules 6/7 do - the per-xApp distinction lives in the
    ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp / ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp
    macros already built for rules 6/7, reused here unchanged.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_profiled_xapp and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    ((ztx_peer_xapp_dest and ztx_allowed_peer_dest_for_xapp) or
     (ztx_ric_platform_dest and ztx_allowed_ric_dest_for_xapp))
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-03 xapp expected peer or ric contact confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, network, normal, audit, profile-match]

- rule: ZTX kpimon-go Expected RIC Platform Contact Confirmed Normal
  desc: >
    kpimon-go connected to a RIC platform service consistent with its
    real observed normal behavior (appmgr registration, e2term RMR
    routing, a1mediator RMR routing) - logged for audit completeness.
    Based on directly watching its real logs this session, not a
    declared profile - kpimon-go has no profile file and is never
    modified. kpimon-go does not get rules 6/7 (see ztx_profiled_xapp),
    so this is its only "confirmed normal" network signal.
  condition: >
    evt.type=connect and
    ztx_in_container and
    ztx_xapp_namespace and
    ztx_kpimon_go_pod and
    container.name = "kpimon-go" and
    fd.typechar in (4, 6) and
    (ztx_dest_e2term or ztx_dest_appmgr or ztx_dest_a1mediator)
  output: >
    ztx_signal=ignored rule_id=ZTX-NORM-04 kpimon-go expected ric platform contact confirmed normal
    (dest=%fd.sip.name:%fd.sport pod=%k8s.pod.name ns=%k8s.ns.name container=%container.name)
  priority: INFORMATIONAL
  tags: [zt-xguard, xapp, kpimon-go, network, normal, audit]
